newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end one pct lower on bonds, banks.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end one pct lower on bonds, banks.

* Toronto stocks fell almost 1.2 percent on Thursday, depressed by weak bonds, bank shares * Decline restrained by strong golds * 108.4 million shrs traded worth C$1.9 billion.
The Toronto stock market ended weaker in brisk trading on Thursday, hit by a sell off in Canadian bonds and heavily weighted bank stocks.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 68.54 points to close at 5842.11, down almost 1.2 percent.
"It was a bond-led downdraft," one trader said of today's market action.

Canadian bonds recorded their biggest one-day drop in more than two years. Investors sold off bonds with Canada/U.S. spreads at near record lows, while a flood of new corporate supply also depressed bonds today, traders said.
A weak Canadian dollar also depressed Canadian bonds. Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$3.17 to C$110.85 to yield 7.086 percent.
"This is a made-in-Canada meltdown," RBC Dominion Securities analyst Dunnery Best said in a market report.

Investors are now likely to buy natural resource stocks after today's heavy selling of financial service issues, one trader said. "This signals a rotation out of the interest sensitives to some more cyclical names," he said.
The trader said investors were moving into gold stocks today, which partly restrained the TSE's fall.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, financial services led the weak side with a 3.65 percent drop -- followed by media, utilities and pipelines. Golds, real estate, and retail rose.
Declining stocks powered ahead of advancing issues 600 to 407, with 284 stocks flat.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce fell 2.50 to 57.00 on 1.7 million shares. Canada's second largest bank reported net profits rose to almost C$1.4 billion for 1996 from C$1.0 billion last year.
Bank of Montreal fell 2.00 to 40.40 on 1.8 million shares.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100))
